patches.value: For i∈K leave W_i fixed if its diameter is positive. If it is a singleton, let U_i be the closed ball centered at its unique point, of diameter min(r/2,(ε2^{-i-3})^{1/q}); n≥1 ensures that ball has exactly this positive diameter.

Choose W from F001. Discard empty members and let K={i:W_i≠∅}. A nonempty zero-diameter W_i is a singleton, since distance zero identifies any two of its points. For each such i take the positive number min(r/2,(ε2^{-i-3})^{1/q}) and replace W_i by the closed ball centered at its unique point, with radius half that number. It has positive diameter at most r and q-cost ≤ε2^{-i-3}<ε2^{-i-2}; the power identity is valid because q>0. The diameter is exactly the prescribed number because n≥1: two opposite points in the first-coordinate direction belong to the closed ball, and the triangle inequality supplies the reverse diameter bound. Leave every positive-diameter member unchanged. Define U_i to be this resulting family on K and r_i=diam(U_i). The cover still contains every W_i and hence covers E, with 0<r_i≤r. Its total q-cost is at most the original cost plus Σ_{i≥0}ε2^{-i-2}≤ original cost+ε/2<ε, using the geometric sum in N001 and finite-partial-sum comparisons. This is the supplied replacement argument with an explicit permissible choice of the small diameters. Discharge L1 and universally quantify q,r,ε.

value.text: Define f_i=ind(J_i∩I,ρ_i^s) on ℝ. Each is measurable: on the Borel set J_i∩I it is a constant and on its Borel complement it is zero; inverse images of Borel sets are therefore one of these sets, ∅, or ℝ. In particular it is λ-almost-everywhere measurable. F002 gives ind(I,c)≤Σ_i f_i pointwise on all ℝ, since outside I both sides vanish.

produces.statement: Every f_i=ind(J_i∩I,ρ_i^s) is measurable and hence λ-almost-everywhere measurable; on all ℝ, ind(I,c)≤Σ_i f_i pointwise.

value.text: M008 applied to the pointwise inequality F003 gives the corresponding inequality of nonnegative integrals. M007 on I with c and N005's λ(I)=1 identifies the left integral with c. M006 exchanges the nonnegative sum and integral, using the measurability already proved in F003; M007 on each J_i∩I with coefficient ρ_i^s then gives c≤Σ_i ρ_i^s λ(J_i∩I). By F002 this is at most Σ_i ρ_i^{s+1}+Σ_i η_iρ_i^s≤Σ_i ρ_i^{s+1}+ε, since η_iρ_i^s=ε2^{-i-1}ρ_i^s/(1+ρ_i^s)≤ε2^{-i-1} and N001 gives Σ_i2^{-i-1}=1. The product and sum comparisons follow first for finite partial sums and then by their suprema; thus they remain valid if a series is infinite. This is Tonelli for nonnegative terms, without finite-integrability premises or an exchange of signed series.

produces.statement: For the arbitrary ε>0 and cover W, c≤Σ_i ρ_i^{s+1}+ε.

value.text: Discharge L3 and quantify ε in F004: for every ε>0, c≤Σ_iρ_i^{s+1}+ε. If the series is infinite, c≤Σ_iρ_i^{s+1} is immediate. Otherwise it is a finite real, and order density applied to the inequality for every ε>0 gives c≤Σ_iρ_i^{s+1}. Since W was an arbitrary δ-cover, c is a lower bound of every admissible (s+1)-cost; therefore c≤H^{s+1}_δ(F), their infimum. Discharge L2, then L1, and universally quantify s,δ. This proves the asserted inequality with exactly the same scale on both sides.

patches.value: F003 is exactly the required global pointwise inequality; its derivation from F002 included the vanishing outside I.
F003 proves every f_i measurable by the inverse-image argument on the Borel pieces J_i∩I and its complement; hence every f_i is λ-almost-everywhere measurable.
